name: Primary Interstitial Lung Disease Specific to Childhood Due to Pulmonary Surfactant Protein Anomalies
aliases: Childhood Interstitial Lung Disease due to Surfactant Protein Deficiency
Surfactant Protein-Related Pediatric Interstitial Lung Disease

criteria.description: Identification of pathogenic variants in surfactant protein genes (SFTPB, SFTPC, ABCA3)
Lung biopsy showing interstitial lung disease with characteristic alveolar proteinosis or fibrosis
Progressive respiratory distress and hypoxemia in infancy or early childhood
High-resolution CT showing ground-glass opacities, interstitial thickening, and cystic changes
Exclusion of other causes of interstitial lung disease such as infection or immunodeficiency

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of pathogenic surfactant protein gene mutation plus compatible clinical and histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is critical for definitive diagnosis; lung biopsy may be required if genetic results are inconclusive.

searchTerms: low oxygen levels not improving with oxygen therapy
oxygen therapy failing to raise blood oxygen

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to chronic respiratory insufficiency
searchTerms: poor growth due to chronic breathing problems
failure to thrive from long-term respiratory issues
growth delay linked to lung insufficiency
bluish skin during feeding or activity
turning blue with exertion or eating
swelling and fatigue from right heart failure

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid
imaging: High-resolution CT showing diffuse ground-glass opacities
Interstitial thickening and cystic changes on chest imaging
genetic: Mutations in SFTPB, SFTPC, or ABCA3 genes
other: Histopathology revealing alveolar proteinosis or interstitial fibrosis
Reduced surfactant protein levels in lung tissue

distinguishingFeatures: Later onset compared to surfactant protein anomalies
History of prematurity and mechanical ventilation
Radiologic findings of airway injury and fibrosis
Absence of surfactant protein gene mutations

redFlags: Rapidly progressive respiratory failure in infancy
Failure to respond to standard oxygen therapy
Family history of neonatal respiratory distress or interstitial lung disease
references: Nogee LM. Genetic causes of surfactant protein deficiencies. Pediatr Pulmonol. 2010;45(5):433-440.
Shulenin S, Nogee LM. Surfactant protein mutations and pediatric interstitial lung disease. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2004;16(3):287-292.
Orphanet: Primary interstitial lung disease specific to childhood due to pulmonary surfactant protein anomalies. ORPHA:100049.
